title: Methods, arguments, and the calculator
summary: Behavior on the object: $this, visibility, static calls, named arguments.

blocks.html:
A property is data. A method is a function that lives inside the class body and works on that data. It reaches the object it was called on through $this, and returns something the caller can use.

That is the whole reason classes exist: the state and the code that understands the state sit in one place, and the outside world asks questions instead of poking at numbers.

blocks.title: a method answers a question
blocks.code:
<?php

class Score
{
    public function __construct(
        public readonly string $label,
        public readonly float $value,
    ) {}

    public function describe(): string
    {
        return $this->label . ' scored ' . $this->value;
    }
}

$quiz = new Score('Quiz', 88.5);

echo $quiz->describe(), "\n";

blocks.html:
describe(): string is a promise: whatever it returns is a string, and the caller can use it without checking. void means it returns nothing on purpose.

The keyword before the name is visibility. public is callable from anywhere. private is callable only from inside the class body, which is how a class hides the steps it used to reach an answer.

blocks.title: a private helper
blocks.code:
<?php

class Score
{
    public function __construct(
        public readonly string $label,
        public readonly float $value,
    ) {}

    public function percentOf(float $max): string
    {
        return $this->label . ': ' . $this->ratio($max) . '%';
    }

    private function ratio(float $max): float
    {
        return round($this->value / $max * 100, 1);
    }
}

$quiz = new Score('Quiz', 88.5);

echo $quiz->percentOf(100), "\n";

blocks.html:
Calling $quiz->ratio(100) from outside is a fatal error, and that is the feature: percentOf() can change how it rounds tomorrow without breaking a caller. Inside the class, $this->ratio() is allowed just like any other method.

Some behavior does not need an object at all. A static method is called on the class, with ::, and it has no $this. Class constants are read the same way, and inside the class body self:: means "this class".

blocks.title: :: on the class itself
blocks.code:
<?php

class Scale
{
    public const PASSING = 60;
    public const MAX = 100;

    public static function describe(float $score): string
    {
        return $score >= self::PASSING
            ? 'passing, out of ' . self::MAX
            : 'failing, needs ' . self::PASSING;
    }
}

echo Scale::describe(76.5), "\n";
echo Scale::describe(41), "\n";
echo Scale::PASSING, "\n";

blocks.html:
Now the caller's problem. new GradeCalculator(90.0, 92.0, 88.0, 95.0) says nothing about which number is which: the constructor decides the order, and a caller who guesses wrong gets a plausible wrong grade.

Named arguments fix that. Write the parameter name, a colon, then the value. Order stops mattering, the call reads like a sentence, and a mistake shows up as an error instead of a bad average.

blocks.title: positional and named, side by side
blocks.code:
<?php

use App\GradeCalculator;

$positional = new GradeCalculator(90.0, 92.0, 88.0, 95.0);
$named = new GradeCalculator(final: 95, midterm: 88, assignment: 92, quiz: 90);

echo $positional->getFinalGrade(), "\n";
echo $named->getFinalGrade(), "\n";
echo $named->getLetterGrade(), ' ', $named->getRemarks(), "\n";

blocks.html:
The rest of the class is four small methods. getWeightedScores() builds two arrays with the same keys, scores and weights, then array_combine(array_keys($scores), array_map(fn($score, $weight) => $score * $weight, $scores, self::WEIGHTS)): two arrays into array_map means the callback gets one element from each, and array_combine pairs the original keys with those products.

getFinalGrade() is array_sum() over that list. getLetterGrade() walks the tiers from 98 down and returns the first one the average reaches. getRemarks() uses match (true), where each arm is a condition and the first true one wins. isPassed() is one comparison.

blocks.title: the machinery, without the class
blocks.code:
<?php

$scores = [
    'quiz' => 90.0,
    'assignment' => 92.0,
    'midterm' => 88.0,
    'final' => 95.0,
];

$weights = [
    'quiz' => 0.20,
    'assignment' => 0.20,
    'midterm' => 0.25,
    'final' => 0.35,
];

$weighted = array_combine(
    array_keys($scores),
    array_map(fn($score, $weight) => $score * $weight, $scores, $weights),
);

print_r($weighted);

$grade = array_sum($weighted);
echo $grade, "\n";

$tiers = [
    ['min' => 92, 'grade' => 'A'],
    ['min' => 90, 'grade' => 'A-'],
    ['min' => 88, 'grade' => 'B+'],
];

foreach ($tiers as $tier) {
    if ($grade >= $tier['min']) {
        echo $tier['grade'], "\n";
        break;
    }
}

echo match (true) {
    $grade >= 90 => 'Excellent',
    $grade >= 80 => 'Good',
    default => 'Failed',
}, "\n";

blocks.title: the whole class, run
blocks.code:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

class GradeCalculator
{
    private const WEIGHTS = [
        'quiz' => 0.20,
        'assignment' => 0.20,
        'midterm' => 0.25,
        'final' => 0.35,
    ];

    private const LETTER_GRADES = [
        ['min' => 98, 'grade' => 'A+'],
        ['min' => 92, 'grade' => 'A'],
        ['min' => 90, 'grade' => 'A-'],
        ['min' => 88, 'grade' => 'B+'],
        ['min' => 84, 'grade' => 'B'],
        ['min' => 80, 'grade' => 'B-'],
        ['min' => 77, 'grade' => 'C+'],
        ['min' => 73, 'grade' => 'C'],
        ['min' => 70, 'grade' => 'C-'],
        ['min' => 60, 'grade' => 'D'],
    ];

    public function __construct(
        private readonly float $quiz,
        private readonly float $assignment,
        private readonly float $midterm,
        private readonly float $final,
    ) {}

    public function getWeightedScores(): array
    {
        $scores = [
            'quiz' => $this->quiz,
            'assignment' => $this->assignment,
            'midterm' => $this->midterm,
            'final' => $this->final,
        ];

        return array_combine(
            array_keys($scores),
            array_map(fn($score, $weight) => $score * $weight, $scores, self::WEIGHTS),
        );
    }

    public function getFinalGrade(): float
    {
        return array_sum($this->getWeightedScores());
    }

    public function getLetterGrade(): string
    {
        $grade = $this->getFinalGrade();

        foreach (self::LETTER_GRADES as $tier) {
            if ($grade >= $tier['min']) {
                return $tier['grade'];
            }
        }

        return 'F';
    }

    public function getRemarks(): string
    {
        return match (true) {
            $this->getFinalGrade() >= 90 => 'Excellent',
            $this->getFinalGrade() >= 80 => 'Good',
            $this->getFinalGrade() >= 70 => 'Fair',
            $this->getFinalGrade() >= 60 => 'Passed',
            default => 'Failed',
        };
    }

    public function isPassed(): bool
    {
        return $this->getFinalGrade() >= 60;
    }
}

$calculator = new GradeCalculator(90.0, 92.0, 88.0, 95.0);

echo $calculator->getFinalGrade(), ' | ',
    $calculator->getLetterGrade(), ' | ',
    $calculator->getRemarks(), ' | ',
    ($calculator->isPassed() ? 'passed' : 'failed'), "\n";

blocks.title: public/gradeCalculator.index.php, reduced to its PHP
blocks.code:
<?php

use App\GradeCalculator;

$calculator = new GradeCalculator(
    quiz: (float)($_POST['quiz_score'] ?? 0),
    assignment: (float)($_POST['assignment_score'] ?? 0),
    midterm: (float)($_POST['midterm_exam'] ?? 0),
    final: (float)($_POST['final_exam'] ?? 0),
);

foreach ($calculator->getWeightedScores() as $part => $points) {
    echo $part, ': ', number_format($points, 2), "\n";
}

echo 'Final Grade: ', number_format($calculator->getFinalGrade(), 2), "%\n";
echo 'Letter Grade: ', $calculator->getLetterGrade(), "\n";
echo 'Remarks: ', $calculator->getRemarks(), "\n";
echo 'Status: ', ($calculator->isPassed() ? 'Passed' : 'Failed'), "\n";

options: The object the method was called on
A copy of the last property written
quiz.why: Each call to $calculator->method() binds $this to that particular object, which is why two objects with the same class keep separate answers.

quiz.q: Which one can be called without ever creating an object?
quiz.why: A static method belongs to the class, so Scale::describe(41) works with no instance. Public instance methods need an object; private ones are not callable from outside at all.

quiz.q: Why prefer new GradeCalculator(quiz: 90, final: 95, midterm: 88, assignment: 92) over the positional form?
options: The order stops mattering and the call names every value
It allows values the constructor does not declare
quiz.why: Named arguments match values to parameters by name, so a reordered call is still correct and a missing or misspelled name is a loud error. Speed is identical.

exercise.brief: Build a GradeCalculator with named arguments: quiz 80, assignment 70, midterm 60, final 90. Print the letter grade, then the remarks, each on its own line.
exercise.starter:

use App\GradeCalculator;

// one calculator, two lines
exercise.hint: The parameter names are quiz, assignment, midterm and final. The class answers with getLetterGrade() and getRemarks().
exercise.solution:

$calculator = new GradeCalculator(
    quiz: 80,
    assignment: 70,
    midterm: 60,
    final: 90,
);
